reader_summary: Before adding data, choose image/request/answer demonstrations that match the desired task. The same visible cat photograph can teach a short Traditional Chinese scene description or a direct counting answer. Text-reading examples need the visible text paired with its transcription; conversation examples need requests paired with useful responses; a recording and transcript teach what was said, not how to respond. Real and synthetic images supply different situations, and copying one question-answer pair changes its weight without adding new situations. The final shop-name exercise is solvable by choosing an image/transcribed-name pair and explaining that the generic label shop cannot teach the name characters.
